이번.forms: 이번이 · 이번에 · 이번 주 · 이번 달
이번.m: this time; this (coming/current) — week, month etc.
이번.x: I'm meeting a friend this weekend.
이번.t: 이번 주 = this week, 다음 주 = next week, 지난주 = last week.

과자.t: 과자 covers packaged snacks — chips, crackers, cookies alike.

연필.t: Count pencils and pens with 자루: 연필 한 자루 (or casually 연필 하나).

이불.x: It was cold, so I slept under a blanket.
이불.e: Slang 이불킥 ('blanket kick') = cringing in bed over an embarrassing memory.
이불.t: 'Cover oneself with a blanket' = 이불을 덮다.

기분.x: I'm in a really good mood today.
기분.t: 기분이 좋아요 = I feel good; 기분이 나빠요 = I'm upset / in a bad mood.

인사.x: I greeted my teacher in the morning.
인사.e: 인사하다 = to greet or bow. Literally 'people matters' — it also means HR (personnel).

인사.ex: 다음 주에 회사 인사 발표가 있어요.
인사.x: The company's personnel announcement is next week.
인사.e: Literally 'people affairs'; the everyday word for 'greeting' is written the same way.
인사.t: 인사 also means 'greeting'; in 인사팀 or 인사 발표 it means personnel.

처음.x: I came to Korea for the first time.
처음.e: 처음 뵙겠습니다 = 'Nice to meet you' (lit. 'I'm seeing you for the first time').
처음.t: Also used as an adverb: 처음 왔어요.

자다.x: I usually go to bed at eleven.
자다.t: 안녕히 주무세요 = 'Good night' to elders; to friends: 잘 자.

퇴근하다.m: to leave work, to get off work
퇴근하다.ex: 오늘은 일이 많아서 늦게 퇴근할 거예요.
퇴근하다.x: I have a lot of work today, so I'll get off late.

기름.m: oil, cooking oil; fat, grease; gasoline
기름.ex: 프라이팬에 기름을 조금 두르고 계란을 부치세요.
기름.x: Put a little oil in the frying pan and fry the egg.
기름.e: Also used for car fuel: 기름을 넣다 means to fill up with gas.
기름.t: 참기름 (sesame oil) and 들기름 (perilla oil) are key flavors in Korean cooking.

오랜만이에요.m: long time no see; it's been a while
오랜만이에요.ex: 민수 씨, 정말 오랜만이에요! 잘 지냈어요?
오랜만이에요.x: Minsu, long time no see! How have you been?
오랜만이에요.e: 오랜만 is short for 오래간만 'after a long while' (오래 'long time').
오랜만이에요.t: Often spelled wrongly as 오랫만; the correct spelling is 오랜만.

천만에요.x: Thanks so much for helping. — You're welcome, anytime.
천만에요.e: 천만 'ten million' — as in 'not in a million years', no thanks needed.
천만에요.t: Textbook-correct but a bit stiff; in daily life Koreans more often reply 아니에요.

새로.forms: 새로 + verb: 새로 사다, 새로 오다
새로.x: I wore the new shoes I bought yesterday.
새로.e: From 새 'new' + -로; compare 새 차 'a new car'.

셀카.ex: 배경이 예뻐서 셀카를 한 장 찍었어요.
셀카.x: The background was pretty, so I took a selfie.
셀카.e: Konglish: short for 셀프 카메라 'self camera', not from English 'selfie'.
셀카.t: Take a selfie: 셀카를 찍다. A selfie stick is 셀카봉.

통역사.x: The interpreter translated Korean into English at the meeting.
통역사.t: 통역 is spoken interpreting; 번역 is written translation.

신고하다.m: to report (to the authorities), to declare
신고하다.x: If there's a fire, call 119 right away.
신고하다.t: Mark the authority with 에: 경찰에 신고하다 (report to the police).

실험.x: We did a fun experiment in science class.
실험.e: Literally 'real test' — checking an idea in practice.
실험.t: Don't mix up with 시험 (exam); 실험 is a lab experiment.

표현하다.x: It's hard to express my feelings in Korean.

연결하다.x: I connected the computer to the internet.

의미하다.x: A red traffic light means stop.
의미하다.e: Literally 'the taste of an idea' — its flavor or sense.
의미하다.t: In everyday talk, 무슨 뜻이에요? 'What does it mean?' is more common than 의미하다.

분노.ex: 사람들은 그 뉴스를 보고 큰 분노를 느꼈습니다.
분노.x: People felt great anger after seeing that news.
분노.e: Two 'anger' syllables stacked together: serious, intense rage.

이모티콘.ex: 답장할 때 귀여운 이모티콘을 자주 써요.
이모티콘.x: I often use cute emoticons when I reply.
이모티콘.t: In Korea it covers emoji and the animated character stickers bought for messenger apps.

벤처.ex: 그는 대학을 졸업하고 벤처 기업을 시작했어요.
벤처.x: After graduating from college, he started a venture company.
벤처.e: From English 'venture'; usually in 벤처 기업, meaning a tech startup.

비정규직.m: non-regular job, temporary or contract position
비정규직.ex: 비정규직 직원들은 월급이 적은 경우가 많아요.
비정규직.x: Non-regular employees are often paid less.
비정규직.e: Literally 'not-regular job' — the opposite of 정규직.
비정규직.t: 정규직 means a permanent, full-time job with benefits; the gap between the two is a big social issue.

손실.x: The typhoon caused heavy losses for farms.
손실.t: 손실 is formal and money-focused; 손해 is the everyday word, e.g. 손해를 보다.

불평등.ex: 남녀 불평등 문제는 아직도 남아 있어요.
불평등.x: The problem of gender inequality still remains.

이슈.ex: 환경 문제가 요즘 큰 이슈가 되고 있어요.
이슈.x: Environmental problems have become a big issue lately.
이슈.e: From English 'issue', but it means a hot topic in the news, not a personal problem.
이슈.t: Don't use 이슈 for personal troubles like 'I have issues'; say 문제 instead.

체질.x: I'm the type of person who feels the cold a lot.
체질.e: Literally 'body nature'; body types are central to traditional Korean medicine.
체질.t: Common pattern '~는 체질이다' = 'I'm the type who…', e.g. 살이 안 찌는 체질.

영양소.x: Vegetables have lots of nutrients that are good for your body.

삐다.x: I fell on the stairs and sprained my ankle.
삐다.t: For a lighter twist, Koreans say 삐끗하다: 허리를 삐끗했어요 'I tweaked my back'.

소변.ex: 검사를 위해 소변을 이 컵에 받아 주세요.
소변.x: Please collect your urine in this cup for the test.
소변.t: 소변 is neutral and medical; 오줌 is the casual word.

상용화.x: This technology will be commercialized within five years.

훼손.x: The damage to nature from the wildfire is serious.
훼손.t: It also covers reputation: 명예 훼손 = defamation.

든든하다.m: reassured, secure; reliable; (of a meal) filling
든든하다.ex: 힘들 때 옆에 친구가 있어서 든든해요.
든든하다.x: I feel reassured having my friend by my side during hard times.
든든하다.t: After a big meal Koreans say 배가 든든해요 (I'm nicely full).

설렘.ex: 새 학기를 앞두고 기대와 설렘으로 잠을 못 잤어요.
설렘.x: Before the new semester, I couldn't sleep from anticipation and excitement.
설렘.e: Noun from 설레다 (to flutter). Spelled 설렘, not 설레임.
설렘.t: Pronounced [설렘] — the ㄹㄹ is a long 'l' sound, not an 'r'.

신경질적.ex: 요즘 일이 많아서 그런지 그가 좀 신경질적이에요.
신경질적.x: Maybe because he has a lot of work these days, he's a bit irritable.
신경질적.e: -적 = '-ic, -al', turning a noun into a descriptor: 신경질적, 낙관적, 희망적.

깐깐하다.ex: 우리 부장님은 깐깐해서 작은 실수도 그냥 넘기지 않아요.
깐깐하다.x: Our manager is so exacting that he doesn't let even small mistakes slide.
깐깐하다.t: 깐깐하다 suggests strict and hard to please; 꼼꼼하다 is the positive 'meticulous'.

천진하다.x: The child smiled brightly with an innocent face.
천진하다.e: Literally 'heaven-given true nature' — untouched by the world.

귀가하다.m: to return home, to go home
귀가하다.ex: 늦게 귀가할 때는 가족에게 미리 연락하세요.
귀가하다.x: When you come home late, let your family know in advance.

완료하다.ex: 모든 작업을 완료하면 저에게 알려 주세요.
완료하다.x: Please let me know when you finish all the work.
완료하다.t: Pronounced [왈료하다] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

논점.m: point at issue, point of argument
논점.x: The main point of that presentation wasn't clear.
논점.t: Pronounced [논쩜]: 점 is tensed in compounds like 장점 and 단점.

우위.ex: 우리 팀이 경기 초반부터 우위를 차지했어요.
우위.x: Our team took the upper hand from the start of the game.

적립금.m: reward points (cash value), store credit; accumulated savings
적립금.ex: 이번 주문에서 적립금 오천 원을 사용했어요.
적립금.x: I used 5,000 won of store credit on this order.
적립금.e: Literally 'money set aside and piled up.'

투고.m: submission, contribution (of writing to a publication)
투고.x: She submitted a poem to a magazine.

노사.ex: 노사 양측이 임금 협상을 다시 시작했습니다.
노사.x: Both labor and management have resumed wage negotiations.

저지하다.m: to stop, to block, to prevent
저지하다.ex: 경찰이 국회로 향하는 시위대의 행진을 저지했습니다.
저지하다.x: The police blocked the protesters' march toward the National Assembly.

발현되다.m: to be manifested, to appear, to be expressed (genes, abilities)
발현되다.ex: 이 유전자는 특정 환경에서만 발현된다고 합니다.
발현되다.x: They say this gene is expressed only in certain environments.
발현되다.e: Literally 'come out and appear' — something latent becoming visible.
발현되다.t: Don't confuse with 발견 (discovery); 발현 means something hidden inside shows itself.

간파하다.m: to see through, to detect, to read (someone's intentions)
간파하다.x: He saw through the other person's scheme at a glance.
간파하다.e: Literally 'look and break through' — seeing past the surface.

대변하다.m: to speak for, to represent; to reflect, to typify
대변하다.ex: 이 노래는 청년 세대의 고민을 잘 대변하고 있어요.
대변하다.x: This song captures the worries of the younger generation well.
대변하다.t: Not 대변 (大便) 'bowel movement' — context matters, and 대변인 is the safe, common derivative.

지대하다.ex: 선생님은 제 인생에 지대한 영향을 주셨어요.
지대하다.x: My teacher had a tremendous influence on my life.
지대하다.t: Almost always appears as 지대한 영향 or 지대한 관심.

가까스로.ex: 뛰어가서 마지막 버스를 가까스로 탈 수 있었어요.
가까스로.x: I ran and barely managed to catch the last bus.
가까스로.t: Synonymous with 겨우 and 간신히, but 가까스로 stresses narrowly escaping failure.

더없이.x: Time with my family is incredibly precious.
더없이.e: Literally 'with nothing more (더)': it can't go any higher.

이율배반.ex: 환경을 지키자면서 일회용품을 쓰는 건 이율배반이에요.
이율배반.x: Saying we should protect the environment while using disposables is a contradiction.
이율배반.e: Literally 'two laws opposing each other'; also the philosophy term for antinomy.

거품을 물다.forms: 거품을 물어요 · 거품을 물었어요 · 입에 거품을 물고
거품을 물다.m: to foam at the mouth; to argue or rant furiously
거품을 물다.ex: 그는 입에 거품을 물고 자기 주장을 했어요.
거품을 물다.x: He argued his point, practically foaming at the mouth.
거품을 물다.e: Literally 'to hold foam in one's mouth,' like English 'foam at the mouth.'

소지.m: room, potential, grounds (for something, usually undesirable)
소지.e: Literally 'plain ground' — the base on which something could grow.
소지.t: Homonym: 소지(所持) means 'possession' (휴대폰 소지). This sense appears in ~의 소지가 있다.

실증적.ex: 이 논문은 실증적 자료를 바탕으로 쓰였습니다.
실증적.x: This paper was written based on empirical data.
실증적.e: Literally 'proving with real things'. -적 = '-ic, -al': 과학적, 경제적.
실증적.t: Use 실증적 directly before a noun, 실증적인 as a modifier, and 실증적으로 as an adverb.

오수.ex: 비가 많이 와서 오수가 도로로 넘쳤어요.
오수.x: It rained so much that dirty water overflowed onto the road.

풍경화.ex: 그 화가는 바다를 그린 풍경화로 유명해요.
풍경화.x: That painter is famous for landscape paintings of the sea.

유화.ex: 유화는 마르는 데 시간이 오래 걸려요.
유화.x: Oil paintings take a long time to dry.

법정대리인.x: A minor needs the consent of a legal representative to sign a contract.
법정대리인.e: Here 법정 means 'set by law', not 'courtroom'; usually a minor's parents.

배임.m: breach of trust, breach of fiduciary duty
배임.ex: 회사 대표가 업무상 배임 혐의로 기소되었습니다.
배임.x: The company's CEO was indicted on charges of occupational breach of trust.
배임.e: Literally 'turning your back on your duty'.
배임.t: Often paired in news as 횡령·배임: embezzlement takes money directly, while 배임 harms the company by abusing your position.

외교문서.x: The government released diplomatic documents that were over 30 years old.

거식증.ex: 무리한 다이어트가 거식증으로 이어질 수 있어요.
거식증.x: Extreme dieting can lead to anorexia.
거식증.t: Pronounced [거식쯩]; its counterpart is 폭식증, and both fall under 식이장애.

쥐불놀이.m: jwibul-nori (swinging fire cans and burning field edges on Daeboreum)
쥐불놀이.x: The kids played jwibul-nori, swinging cans of fire around.
쥐불놀이.e: 쥐 (rat) + 불 (fire) + 놀이 (game): burning field edges to drive out rats and pests.
쥐불놀이.t: Pronounced [쥐불로리] — ㄹ followed by ㄴ becomes ㄹㄹ.

수호하다.m: to guard, to defend, to protect

사회적 약자.ex: 정부는 사회적 약자를 위한 지원을 늘렸습니다.
사회적 약자.x: The government increased support for the socially disadvantaged.

지열.ex: 아이슬란드는 지열을 이용해 난방을 많이 합니다.
지열.x: Iceland uses a lot of geothermal heat for heating.

할애하다.m: to set aside, to devote, to spare (time or space)
할애하다.ex: 그는 바쁜 중에도 봉사 활동에 시간을 할애했습니다.
할애하다.x: Despite being busy, he set aside time for volunteer work.
할애하다.e: Literally 'cut away something cherished' — giving up precious time or space.

고고하다.m: lofty and aloof, noble and solitary
고고하다.ex: 그는 평생 돈과 권력을 멀리하며 고고하게 살았어요.
고고하다.x: He lived a lofty life, keeping money and power at a distance.
고고하다.e: Literally 'alone and high' — standing above worldly concerns.
